segments.text: Hey friends, You often **overestimate** what you can achieve in six days, but you
**hugely underestimate** what you can accomplish in six months. In just six
months, you can completely change your life —
and I guarantee that. Yes, maybe you’ve tried before.
This New Year, you might have made some resolutions — like going to the
gym, reading books, or waking up early. Maybe you couldn’t stick to them.
Maybe you started but gave up along the way.
And now you’re feeling guilty or regretful about it. But don’t worry —
all of that can change. And for that, I’m giving you a bold challenge.
The plan I’m going to share with you today — if you follow even a part
of it sincerely — can completely transform your life in the next six months. And
if it doesn’t, you
can stop watching my videos, unsubscribe, or even leave angry comments — I
won’t mind. Now you might wonder — why am I making such a big promise?
Because what I’m about to share with you isn’t just something I read in a book.
I’m not saying it just to make the script sound good. The things I’m going
to talk about today are things I’ve personally applied in my own life
to bring about real transformation. And over the
next six months, I’ll be applying these same principles right alongside you.
This isn’t just a motivational video or a book summary. Today’s video is a
**Six-Month Life Transformation Challenge** — One habit,
one goal, one mission every month. Six habits in six months, and a brand new life
— that’s the promise. If you commit to this, within just one
month, your focus and consistency will become sharper than a blade.
By **Month Two**, you’ll start gaining a level of clarity like you’ve never
experienced before. By the **Third Month**, you’ll have broken
free from the trap of perfectionism, and taking action will become effortless
for you. By the **Fifth Month**, you’ll have developed the emotional strength
within you — so much so that you won’t need to push yourself every single day.
Your goals will start pulling you toward them. By the **fifth month**, you’ll
begin to look completely transformed — both physically and mentally. People
around you will start asking, *“How did you bring about such a big change?”* And
by the **sixth month**, you’ll have built a **new identity**. Your self-doubt will
be gone, and you will have **unlocked your true potential**. I’m
ready to apply this Six-Month Transformation Plan in my own life.
If you’re ready too, then comment below saying **”Yes, I accept this challenge”**
— and make sure to include today’s date. That way, six months from now, you can
come back here and see the difference within yourself and truly measure
your growth. Now, why six months? Because a year often feels too long, and
a month feels too short. Yes, monthly goals bring a lot of excitement —
Changes will start happening in your life too. For example —
last month, I gave myself a challenge.
Before that, I looked like *this*, and after the challenge, I lost 5
kilos and started looking like *this*. Now, if you look closely, I went
through a lot of **internal changes**, but
the **visible changes** aren’t that dramatic — yet.
And related to this, when I asked my trainer how long it would take to see
really noticeable changes in my body, he said the same thing — *“Give your body
at least six months.”* In fact, **Jim Rohn**, who was Tony Robbins’ mentor,
also says that *six months
is the sweet spot*. It’s not too long, and it’s not too short — it’s just right.
To bring a **drastic transformation** in your life, let’s understand with a
small example: If you read just 10 pages a day, you may not notice a
big change in yourself right away. But if you do it consistently for six months,
you’ll have read **1,800 pages** — That’s about **6 to 7
life-changing books** completed. Similarly, if you
work out for just 20 minutes a day, you might not see a huge difference
in a month… But in **six months**, the results can be massive.
That’s **3,600 minutes** — which equals **60 hours** of working out. And that’s a
*lot*! Remember this — **small, daily actions** can lead to **massive life
changes**, *if* you stay consistent with them. That’s why it’s so important
to understand the power of the **compounding effect**,
which we’re going to apply over the next six months. Six
months is not some imaginary timeline — it’s *real* and *doable*.
Data shows that in six months, you can effectively change your **routine**, your
**habits**, and even your **mindset**. Because yes — in one month, you might
take up a habit out of excitement, but it can also fade away just as quickly.
However, if you stick to a habit for six months, your brain gets **solidly
rewired**, and the chances of you quitting that habit become almost zero.
That’s why remember this quote: **“Life doesn’t change by chance, it changes
by design.”** And to change that design, **motivation alone
won’t be enough**. This is where the real problem lies — Many times, we fail
in life because we try to take action based purely on **motivation**. But
motivation is just like a **Diwali rocket** — The kind you light up, and
it bursts brilliantly... for a moment.
But after a while, it’s dark again.
Everything’s gone. That’s why, so often, you watch a video on YouTube, see a
reel, come across something inspiring — you like it, maybe even save
it… But when it’s actually time to **take action**, you don’t. And then,
there are no results. Maybe something similar happened **six months ago** too.
At the beginning of the year, you probably set some goals. You thought
you’d do something meaningful...
but because you didn’t have a **proper
plan**, **clear systems**, or **real accountability**, you haven’t
been able to achieve those things you truly wanted to do. In this video,
we’ll learn how to **plan your life**, and how to create a **simple system**
for yourself — the same kind of system I’ve created and used for my own journey.
It brought **dramatic changes** within me. So, without any further ado, let’s
get to the plan. Now I’m going to share my **simple plan** with you. It’s
simple — but don’t mistake it for being weak. It’s actually **very powerful**.
Simple things are what our mind can follow regularly — and that’s how
consistency is built. But when things get complex, our mind tends to avoid
them — and that’s when consistency breaks. Now watch what I’m going to do.
Basically, we’ll divide this **six-month challenge** into **monthly
challenges**. Each month,
we’ll focus on building **just one habit** and developing it fully. That’s
it — just **one**. Why only one? Because I’ve experienced it myself — and
I’m sure you have too — when you try to bring too many habits into your life
at once, you might manage for a few days, but it doesn’t last for long.
But on the other hand, if you focus on **just one habit**, it becomes much
easier to build that habit — and the results are very **distinct and
noticeable**, which is also explained in *Atomic Habits*. That’s exactly
what happened with me. Last month, when I gave myself
a **mini one-month challenge**, I decided on just one thing — that I would go
to the gym and train with a trainer. And just by committing
to that one thing, what happened? Gradually, I also started eating healthy.
I started walking as well. I didn’t have it in my mind that I *had* to do all
these things — but just by focusing on **one habit**, other good habits
started coming to me **automatically**, one after another.
That’s how it works. So this month, I’ve decided that in the coming month,
I’ll **read a book every day** and **share one lesson from it on Instagram**
— because I know that most people struggle to read books themselves.
Now, this habit is very important for my **mental fitness** — and also for
my **financial growth**. That’s why I’m going to take on this challenge. And
one more important thing
— I take these challenges in **21-day blocks**. Why is that? Because if we
try to commit to something for a full 30 days straight, it can
start to feel a bit overwhelming and pressurizing.
Why is that? Because the
book **Psycho-Cybernetics** says that your brain needs **at
least 21 days** to become familiar with any new habit or change. That’s
why I’ve structured it this way — **21 days of action**, followed by a
**9-day gap**. What happens in those 9 days? They allow me to
go **all in** with full focus and intensity during the 21
days — knowing that a
short break is coming.
Like going to the gym or working on my health — but then, during those **9
days**, I allow myself to **relax a bit**. I don’t drop the habit
completely, but I
do **release the pressure** I had put on myself. So it creates a really
**beautiful system**. And if you
think about it — it just makes sense. Now here’s what **you need to do**…
In the next six months, focus on building **one new habit each month**. Feel the
change it brings — if it feels right, keep it. If it doesn’t, move on
to another habit. By doing this, over six months, you’ll build **six powerful
habits** that will give you a **brand new life**. This process will help you
build a **routine** — one that gives you both **discipline** and **freedom**.
I’ll also be sharing **12 habits** with you. You don’t have
to follow all
12 — just pick **any 6 habits** that resonate with you. Comment below
and let me know **which 6 habits** you’re going to follow in your life.
Alright, let’s start with the 12 habits. **Habit No.
1: Wake up early** — Books
like *The 5 AM Club* and *The Miracle Morning* explain
how waking up early can be incredibly beneficial for us.
But here’s the thing — the problem I see with the **5 AM Club** is this: If you
usually wake up at 8 or 10 in the morning, and suddenly you try to start waking up
at 5 AM, it’s going to be **very tough**.
Whereas, the book **Atomic Habits** says that to build a habit,
you should keep things **simple and easy**. So, what should you do instead?
You **don’t need to start waking up at 5 AM**. All you need to do
is wake up **just one hour earlier** than your current wake-up time — that’s it.
Or maybe two hours earlier, if you prefer. For example, I used to wake up
at 8 AM, but now I’ve started waking up at 6 AM. So if you also used to wake
up at 8, and you simply start waking up at 7 AM, what happens then?
In six months, just by waking up **one hour earlier**, you’ll
gain **180 extra hours**. Now think about what all you can do in those 180
hours — you can learn a new skill, read books, bring about a real transformation
in your life. This habit alone
can be **incredibly powerful** for you. Because remember: **Winners don’t wake
up late.** Now, the next habit on the list is: **Read daily**. There was a
man named **Moore**, who was once homeless and going through a really tough life…
He then started developing one habit from within — the habit of **daily reading**.
He began reading every single day. And what happened as a result? His brain
became so **sharp and intelligent** that **Harvard** itself offered him
a **scholarship** and invited him to study there. That completely changed
his life. In the same way, if **you** start reading just **10 pages a day**,
then as I mentioned earlier — in six months, you’ll have finished **6 to 7
amazing books** that can bring **drastic changes** to your life.
Remember — **Books compress decades into days.** The next habit is:
**Exercise**. There was a 17-year-old boy named **Marcus Skeet** who suffered
from severe **depression**, **anxiety**, **OCD**, and even **type 2 diabetes**.
To fight these problems, he started exercising — specifically, he
began **running**. In the beginning, it was **very difficult** for him. But
as the weeks went by, his **energy started increasing**… His **clarity** and
**confidence** started to grow. He became so powerful — both mentally and
physically — that he ended up **running the entire length of Britain**, covering
**874 miles**. As a result, he lost **36 kilos** and raised **157,000 euros**
for a charity. Remember this: **If you don’t make time for exercise, you will
eventually have
to make time for illness.** The next habit is: **Writing or Journaling**.
**Tim Ferriss**, the author of amazing books like *The 4-Hour
Workweek* and *Tools of Titans*, and
a successful entrepreneur, used
to struggle a lot with **anxiety** and **overthinking**.
That’s when he started **writing daily**
— just a few minutes every morning after waking up. And what happened as a
result of this one habit? His mind, which was often confused
and cluttered, started gaining **clarity**. His anxiety began to
fade. He actually credits this **one single habit** as one
of the **biggest reasons** behind his success and his **strong mental health**.
Remember — one of **Tim Ferriss’s** own quotes: **”I don’t write to
be productive, I journal to be sane.”** Next habit: **Gratitude Practice**.
**Shawn Achor**, a Harvard researcher and author of the book *The
Happiness Advantage*, conducted a study where students were placed under **extreme
academic pressure**. Then, he asked them to do a **simple gratitude exercise**
— Every day, they had to **write down three things** they were grateful
for, and continue this for **21 days**. So what were the results?
The students’ **happiness levels** started increasing, their **stress levels**
went down, and their **productivity improved**.
And the best part? Even after they **stopped the exercise** after 21
days, the **positive effects were still visible**. Remember: **What
you appreciate, appreciates.** Next habit: **Eat Clean**. **Joe Cross**,
an Australian entrepreneur, was **obese** — his weight had gone above **300 lbs**.
He was also diagnosed with a **rare autoimmune disease**. So what did
he do?
Just **one thing** — he started focusing on **eating healthy**. And what was
the result? By simply changing his diet, he lost **100 lbs**, **stopped
all medications**,
**reversed all his diseases**, and even **documented** his entire journey.
He made a film called **“Fat, Sick & Nearly Dead”**, which inspired
**millions** of people to start eating healthier. Remember: **You are what
you eat.** Avoid fast, fake, and easy food — even if it looks tempting.
Next habit: **Digital Detox**. **Cal Newport**, author of *Digital
Minimalism*, studied many professionals who were addicted to screens. One of
them was a **software engineer**, who completely cut down his screen time for
just **30 days**. He replaced that time with **journaling** and
**walking**. As a result, he reported that his **focus became much deeper**.
His **sleep improved**, and his **anxiety levels reduced**.
Remember what **Cal Newport** says: **”The cost of being constantly connected
is the life you’re not living.”** Next habit: **Planning the Day**. **Brian
Tracy**, the legendary productivity coach, says: If you develop just one simple
habit — writing down your **plan for the next day** every
night before going to bed — your **execution** will significantly improve.
Your **execution will improve by more than 25% every single day**, and
this has even been backed by client testimonials.
One of Brian Tracy’s clients was a struggling sales executive who adopted
this habit — and within just **six months**, he **doubled his income**.
He said this habit was absolutely **life-changing** for him.
Remember: **“Every minute spent in planning saves ten in execution.”**
Next habit: **Affirmations**.
**Louise Hay**, author of *You Can Heal Your Life*,
said that daily affirmations helped her tremendously in **fighting cervical
cancer**. What she basically did was practice **affirmations around forgiveness
and emotional healing**. This started to **shift her energy**, began
to **resolve her problems**, and helped **reduce her stress** significantly.
Because of this, she said, **“I was able to treat my cancer without surgery.”**
And not just that — her work has since helped **millions of people heal** around
the world. Next habit, closely related to this: **Visualization**.
**Olympic athletes** regularly use visualization
as a part of their mental training. Even **Virat Kohli**, **Cristiano Ronaldo**,
and **Michael Phelps**
— Speaking of Michael Phelps, he is the **most decorated Olympian** in history.
He would often do **mental rehearsals** — visualizing every **stroke**, every
**turn**, and every possible situation that could occur. He even practiced
this **before sleeping**, and his **coach made him do
it regularly**. So in the **2008 Olympics**, when his **goggles filled
with water**, he was still able to perform — because he had already
**visualized that exact situation** in advance.
That’s why he didn’t panic — and
in that moment, he **set a record** and **won the gold medal**.
**Oprah Winfrey** says, **“If you can
see it and believe it, it’s a
lot easier to achieve it.”** Next habit: **Deep Connections**. **Dr.
Dean Ornish**, a renowned heart disease specialist, conducted a study on patients
with severe heart issues. He found that while those who **reversed their heart
conditions** did pay attention to **exercise** and **diet**, there was
also **one common and very important factor** they all had in common… And
that was: **Deep emotional connection**. The people who regularly spent time
with **those they loved**, who had **someone they could openly share their
feelings with** — those individuals **recovered much faster** and **improved
their health** significantly,
compared to those who were relying **only on medication**. **Dr.
Dean Ornish** says: **“The opposite of loneliness is not company — it’s
connection.”** Next habit: **Side Hustle**. **Sara Blakely**, who
once sold fax machines door-to-door like a salesperson, used to work on her **side
idea** every night after finishing her regular job. Her side idea was a
**footless pantyhose**, and she worked on it consistently. It took her around
a year — but from that very idea, she eventually **gave birth to Spanx**.
**Spanx** was the company she founded, into which she initially invested
just **\$5,000**. She had **no background in fashion**, but
she stayed **consistently committed** to working on her side hustle. And
because of this **one habit**, she went on to become the **youngest self-made
female billionaire**.
One of her quotes is: **”Don’t quit your day job until your night job
pays.”** So now, as you can see — I’ve shared everything with you.
What to do, why to do it, and how to do it — you’ve got the answers to **all
these questions** in this video. Now it’s **your turn**.
Go ahead and **comment below** to commit: **“Yes, I’m
taking this 6-month challenge.”** Write down today’s **date**, and
also list the **6 habits** you’ve chosen to follow over the next six months.
You might not be **110% sure** right now — and that’s okay. But still, go ahead
and **write down your 6 habits**. I’ll be sharing
mine with you as well, especially on **Instagram**,
since I’ve been more active there lately. I’ll be posting videos and updates based
on that platform. I’ll also upload these videos on my other channel,
**Zeeshan Shaikh Shorts** — so you can check them out there too.
If you’re not on Instagram, no worries — you’ve got these two other options. But
if you’re **really serious** about taking this challenge, then I **highly
recommend** you join my **WhatsApp community**. That
way, I can regularly share my **progress** with you. And if any opportunities come
up where I go **live** and connect directly with you, you’ll get updates
about those through the WhatsApp community as well.
So make sure to join — otherwise, you might end up **missing out**.
Alright, remember — this wasn’t just a video, it was a **challenge**. And
if you’ve stayed till the end, I
know for sure that **you’re going to take it**. I believe in you, and you should
believe in yourself too. Six months from now, you’ll truly **thank yourself**
— and you’ll have an **incredible story** to tell. Because **discipline** can
be measured in **grams**, but **regret** weighs in **tons**.
We don’t want to end up in **regret** — we want to walk the path
of **discipline**. So come on, let’s **write the next
six months together** — amazing stories for you, and for
me too. I’m **Zeeshan Shaikh**, and you’re watching **Seeken**. This
was your **wake-up call for a better life**.
**Bye-bye!**
